entries.name: Theodore Gibson

expected.charges: Contempt of the Florida Legislative Investigating ('Johns') Committee
expected.sentence:
Cited for contempt; fought the anti-NAACP probe to the Supreme Court

Charges as recorded: Contempt of the Florida Legislative Investigating ('Johns') Committee — refusing to produce NAACP membership lists

updates.convicted: Contempt judgment reversed by the U.S. Supreme Court on March 25, 1963.
updates.sentence: Six months in prison and a $1,200 fine, with an additional six months if the fine was not paid. The U.S. Supreme Court reversed the contempt judgment on March 25, 1963. Actual service of the sentence has not been established.

entries.name: Martin Popper

expected.sentence:
Six months in prison and a $500 fine

Verdict as recorded: Convicted on four counts (1961)

Charges as recorded: Contempt of Congress — refusing to answer HUAC

updates.convicted: Convicted in 1961; judgment reversed on July 5, 1962.
updates.sentence: Six months in prison and a $500 fine imposed June 23, 1961. The appellate court reversed the judgment on July 5, 1962 because the indictment was insufficient. Actual imprisonment under this sentence has not been established.
